title: Tenant commit onboarding: capacity safeguard & zero-day plan
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary

This playbook describes the capacity safeguard checklist and a zero-day operational plan for tenant commit onboarding (Dedicated / Reserved pools). It is intended for platform operators, SREs, and customer success engineers who accept or enable committed capacity for customers. The goal is to ensure predictable performance and avoid downstream overload during first-week traffic spikes.

Scope and applicability

- Applies to: Dedicated pools, reserved tenant slots, private VPC deployments when committing GPU capacity for a customer.
- Not applicable to: Hosted multi-tenant buckets without commit, purely experimental onboarding without SLA.
- Risk profile covered: sudden token surges, warmup latency, KV/prefix cache cold starts, packer/worker OOMs, autoscaler misconfigurations.

Owner and escalation paths

- Primary owner: Platform Capacity team (oncall: platform-capacity-primary)
- Secondary owner: Platform SRE (oncall: platform-sre)
- Customer escalation: Customer Success Manager (CSM) then Enterprise Support (enterprise-support)
- Out-of-band escalation: Pager to Platform Pager (P0) if sustained SLO violation > 30 minutes

Pre-onboarding checklist (must be completed before commit date)

1) Capacity reservation verification
   - Confirm tenant ID and reservation ID in capacity ledger.
   - Check reservation matches promised GPU type (e.g., A10G / H100) and count.
   - Validate region placement and affinity rules.

2) Model & variant readiness
   - Confirm model binaries exist and are registered in runtime catalog with pinned version.
   - Verify quantization profile (FP16/INT8) and runtime kernel compatibility.

3) Traffic profile & SLAs
   - Obtain expected QPS, median/95/99 latency targets, and token/s per second.
   - Collect synthetic prompt mix: short chat p50, long generation p95, embeddings ratio.

4) Warmset seeding plan
   - Define KV prefix lists to seed into cache. Attach sample prefixes file to onboarding ticket.

5) Monitoring & dashboards
   - Ensure dedicated tenant dashboard exists: token-rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU util, batch-size distribution, KV cache hit-rate, OOM/sec, model-swap errors.
   - Ensure alerting covers both symptom and cause (see Alerts table below).

6) Canary and soft-launch plan
   - Configure canary route: 5% traffic for first 15 minutes, 25% for first 4 hours, then progressive ramp.

Onboarding day zero-day runbook (operational steps)

Pre-launch (T-48 to T-1 hours)

- T-48: Confirm all checks from pre-onboarding checklist are green. Run synthetic workload locally (see Appendix A).
- T-12: Provision burst buffer credits and confirm autoscaler warm pools > 1.
- T-2: Create operator slack channel with SRE, capacity, CSM, and customer technical lead.
- T-0: Lock commit migration window and set console routes to canary policy.

Launch phases (timed, operator actions)

1) Phase 1 — Canary (0–15 min)
   - Route 5% of production traffic.
   - Operator actions: watch p95 latency, batch-size, and KV cache hit-rate.
   - If p95 latency > target or OOM spikes > 1/min: Roll back to pre-commit variant and notify owners.

2) Phase 2 — Initial ramp (15min–4h)
   - Route 25% traffic.
   - Validate batch growth remains < configured max (default 512 tokens/batch).
   - Validate model swap success rate >= 99.5%.

3) Phase 3 — Progressive scale (4h–24h)
   - Ramp to 50% and observe production characteristics.
   - If backend GPU utilization consistently > 85% for > 10m, open scaling action: add one warm node per 100 QPS or apply burst credit.

4) Phase 4 — Full commit (24h+)
   - Route 100% only after 24h of stable metrics and no SLO violations.

Immediate mitigation checklist (when SLOs degrade)

1) Symptom triage (first 5 minutes)
   - Identify dominant signal: latency, OOMs, error-rate, queue depth.
   - Confirm whether problem is tenant-specific (single tenant dashboard) or platform-wide.

2) Fast actions (operator can execute)
   - Toggle canary to 0% (quick rollback).
   - Disable batching (set batching_factor=1) for offending route to reduce pressure on batching/kv logic.
   - Toggle to a lower-cost model variant (smaller model) if available.

3) Intermediate actions (5–30 minutes)
   - Increase warm pool size / evict spot-backends per predictive-scaler guidance.
   - Inject synthetic warmups to KV cache for heavy prefixes.

4) Extended actions (>30 minutes)
   - Execute tenant-level rate limit (soft quota) and coordinate with CSM to throttle client.
   - If sustained OOMs persist, trigger emergency model swap to CPU-backed fallback (latency penalty expected).

Alerts and dashboard specifications

- Alert: tenant-p95-latency-burn
  - Trigger: p95 latency exceeds SLA by 30% for 5 minutes.
  - Pager: platform-sre P1, capacity oncall.

- Alert: gpu-oom-spike
  - Trigger: >3 OOMs across the tenant pool in 10 minutes.
  - Pager: platform-capacity.

- Alert: kv-cache-hitrate-drop
  - Trigger: KV hit-rate falls below 60% and token-rate > baseline for 10 minutes.
  - Pager: platform-operator (email).

Recommended dashboard widgets

| Widget | Primary metric | Threshold to watch | Owner |
|-------|----------------|--------------------|-------|
|Traffic heatmap| tokens/sec (tenant) | n/a | Capacity team|
|Latency histogram| p50/p95/p99 | p95 SLA line | SRE|
|Batch distribution| tokens per batch | > configured max | Runtime team|
|GPU utilization| % util per machine | >85% sustained | Capacity|
|KV cache heat| hit-rate by prefix | <60% | Runtime ops|

Validation and acceptance tests (operational)

- Synthetic smoke test: run 1k short generation requests, assert p95 < SLA and error-rate < 0.1%.
- Warmset validation: verify at least 75% of promoted prefixes have hit-rate > 70% within 30 minutes.
- Eviction simulation: run controlled eviction test to ensure autoscaler behaves and warm pool rebuilds in < 15 minutes.

Post-onboarding retrospective template (to fill 48–72 hours after full commit)

1) Executive summary (1 paragraph)
2) Timeline of events (with timestamps and actors)
3) Metrics observed vs expected (attach dashboard links)
4) Root cause analysis for any deviation
5) Action items (owner, ETA, validation criteria)
6) Customer impact summary and communication log

Runbook maintenance and cadence

- Owner must review this document quarterly and after every onboarding that required rollbacks.
- Add new failure signatures observed to the alert list and include sample traces.

Appendix A — CLI & test snippets

- Warmset seeding example (curl):
  curl -X POST https://internal.api/kv/seed -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"tenant":"TENANT_ID","prefixes":["/user/","/chat/" ] }'

- Synthetic load example (python):
  from requests import post
  for _ in range(1000):
    post('https://api.redwood.internal/generate', json={"tenant":"TENANT_ID","prompt":"Hello"})

Appendix B — Recommended config matrix

| Item | Recommended default | Rationale |
|------|--------------------|-----------|
|batching_factor|max 512 tokens | Prevents massive memory amplification |
|warm_pool_min|2 nodes | Avoids cold-starts for small commitments |
|burst_credit|25% of monthly commit | Handles first-week spikes |
|kv_prefetch_window|30 minutes | Sufficient to populate common prefixes |

Appendix C — Examples of common failure signatures and playbook references

- OOM cascade during long generation: see runbook /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/partial-kv-cache-corruption-reconstitution-and-retrospective-2026
- Rapid token burst with KV-miss amplification: see /confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/cache-prefetch-prioritization-for-llm-workloads-2026

Contact list

- Platform Capacity (oncall): platform-capacity-primary@redwood.internal
- Platform SRE (oncall): platform-sre@redwood.internal
- CSM escalation: enterprise-csm@redwood.internal
